messages:
maya: Heads-up: canary show a p99 blip after yesterday's multi-variant routing tweak. Looks related to compat-set fanout + fallbacks.

sam: I pulled profiler traces at 10:20 UTC. p50 stable, p95 +4ms, p99 +18ms for model-family-B text-gen. Throughput unchanged. Flame graph: https://internal/profiler/edgecase/1885

linh: My bet is batching fragmentation. When requests for the same route hit different variants (quant vs fp16) they don't coalesce well -> smaller batches + kernel change overhead.

rachel: Also seeing KV cache churn. KV hit-rate on canary nodes dropped 0.83 -> 0.62. Fallbacks are missing local KV layouts and triggering rebuilds.

sam: Example trace snippet:
```
Req1: route=X variant=v1-4bit
Req2: route=X variant=v2-fp16 (fallback)
Scheduler: forms [Req1] then [Req2]
Runtime: selects fp16 kernel
KV: Req1 misses due to layout mismatch -> warmup
```
So we pay twice: less efficient batching + KV warmup latency.

maya: That matches my read. Current permissive compat routing falls back eagerly to fp16 to reduce single-request latency, but it harms batch economics under mixed traffic.

linh: Proposal: introduce a short "variant-hold" window (e.g., 8ms) where we prefer grouping same-variant requests before merging across variants. Also add token_budget_target per-variant so small-variant batches don't ship too early.

Sketch config:
```
batching: {
  variant_prefer_window_ms: 8,
  token_budget_target: { "v1-4bit": "2048", "v2-fp16": "4096" }
}
```

rachel: For KV: make cache keys variant-aware (sticky entries) and prefetch compatible fallback layouts for high-fanout routes to avoid misses during rollouts.

sam: On the kernel side, mixing quant and fp16 in same batch forces format conversion/serialization path. Prefer same-kernel batches even if that adds a few ms queue wait.

maya: Action items:
- A: Enable variant_prefer_window_ms=8 + token_budget_target per-variant on canary. Owner: linh
- B: Variant-aware KV sticky keys + prefetch for top-50 routes. Owner: rachel
- C: Microbench run to measure p99, KV hit-rate, batch-size distribution pre/post. Owner: sam
- D: Canary for 12h, auto-revert if p99 > baseline +10ms. Owner: maya

deploy-bot: Canary PR queued: canary/variant-batching-tune #PR-482 deployed to canary pool at 1885004355

linh: PR pushed with conservative defaults. Added telemetry: per-compat-set coalescing_ratio and kernel_switch_count/min.

sam: I'll add dashboard cards: compat_coalesce_rate, kernel_switch_rate, kv_warmup_rate and wire alerts for regressions.

rachel: One more idea: disable cross-variant fallback for very short responses (<=32 tokens). Warmup cost dominates for those.

maya: Good—add a canary flag `no_fallback_under_tokens: 32`.

linh: Done, included `no_fallback_under_tokens: 32` in the PR.

sam: Local perf harness results: on mixed traffic median batch size rose 3.2 -> 4.8, KV hit-rate recovered to 0.80, p99 reduced by ~9ms on probe workload.

rachel: I'll script the KV prefetch and a synthetic to validate correctness under layout changes.

maya: If canary holds, roll to dedicated pools with policy tunables per-customer. High-privacy customers can keep more aggressive fallbacks.

sam: Posting incremental perf numbers in 3h. Keeping change conservative for now.

maya: Summary pinned: variant_prefer_window_ms=8, token_budget targets per-variant, no_fallback_under_tokens=32, variant-aware KV + prefetch, 12h canary. Checkback in 6h.
